threads.body:
These suites are Testcontainers tests themselves — `AbstractVaadinTest` starts a `BrowserWebDriverContainer("selenium/standalone-chrome:4.43.0")`, and `vaadin-14.2:testing` depends on `org.testcontainers:testcontainers-selenium`. Replacing `testcontainersBuildService` instead of adding to it takes these tasks out of the repo-wide cap of 2 concurrent container tests, so a vaadin suite can now run alongside 2 other container-heavy suites rather than counting toward that limit.

A task can declare more than one shared service, and Gradle makes it hold a lease on each one before it runs, so declaring both keeps the resource cap and adds the serialization you want here:

```suggestion
    usesService(gradle.sharedServices.registrations["testcontainersBuildService"].service)
    usesService(vaadinBuildService)
```

(Checked this on a scratch build: with a max-2 service used by three tasks and a max-1 service used by two of them, the two sharing the max-1 service never overlapped while the third still ran in parallel.)
